team-checkpoint.description: Shared team-checkpoint roster oracle (TEAM MODE P4). Folds an identical seeded per-HAID checkpoint stream through the implementation (bin/lib/checkpoint_share.fold_stream) and an independently-authored reference fold, normalizes both to a common comparable partition (served roster set keyed by HAID + security-exclusion count — NOT the raw records), and asserts they are identical across all seeds. Catches whole-aggregate privacy/roster bugs a per-record property check passes: a security-lane leak (INV-C), a secret leak (INV-B), a consent-off leak (INV-D), an absolute-path leak (INV-A), or a dropped/duplicated/misattributed teammate (INV-G).

assets.name: reference-fold
assets.purpose: Independently authored, spec-only recomputation of the checkpoint roster fold over a seeded synthetic checkpoint stream. Imports nothing from bin/lib/* (every constant and rule reproduced from INVARIANTS.md), so it shares no code path with the implementation under test.

assets.name: seeded-checkpoint-stream
assets.purpose: Deterministic seeded per-HAID checkpoint stream generator (reference.generate_stream). Same seed => byte-identical stream; the distribution is skewed so a slice is security-sensitive (INV-C exclusion) and a slice is consent-off (INV-D skip), the rest served.

issue-collection.description: Anonymized issue-collection k-anon aggregate oracle. Feeds an identical seeded issue_v1 stream through the implementation aggregate (bin/lib/cp_issue_aggregate.py) and an independently-authored reference aggregator, normalizes both to a common comparable partition (served bucket set + suppressed bucket set + security-exclusion count — NOT the raw envelopes, which differ by design), and asserts they are identical across all seeds. Catches whole-output k-anon/bucketing/security-exclusion bugs a per-bucket property check passes.

assets.name: reference-aggregator
assets.purpose: Independently authored, spec-only recomputation of the k-anon issue aggregate over a seeded synthetic issue stream. Imports nothing from bin/lib/* (every constant and computation reproduced from INVARIANTS.md), so it shares no code path with the implementation under test.

assets.name: seeded-issue-stream
assets.purpose: Deterministic seeded issue_v1 stream generator (reference/aggregate_ref.generate_stream). Same seed => byte-identical stream driving the differential comparison; the distribution is skewed so some signature buckets clear the k>=10 distinct-team floor and some do not, and a slice is security-sensitive (exercising INV-F exclusion).

emulator-gb.description: Game Boy (DMG / LR35902 CPU) emulator oracle. Verifies an implementation by diffing its per-instruction execution trace against a known-correct reference trace, then asserting the standard Blargg ROM serial-output pass markers.

assets.name: blargg-cpu-instrs
assets.purpose: Blargg's cpu_instrs test ROM suite — the de-facto correctness battery for CPU opcode/flag behavior. Each sub-ROM prints PASS/FAIL over the serial link.
assets.fetch: git submodule or curl per-rom; do NOT copy ROM bytes into this repo

assets.name: gameboy-doctor-truth-traces
assets.purpose: gameboy-doctor reference CPU state logs (one line per instruction: registers + PC + opcode bytes). The trace-diff compares the implementation's emitted log line-for-line against these.
assets.fetch: clone reference repo; truth logs live under its truth/ tree, keyed by test rom number

exchange-lob.description: Limit-order-book matching-engine oracle. Replays seeded order flow through both the implementation and an independent naive O(n^2) reference matcher, then asserts the resulting fills, book state, and event streams are identical across all seeds.

assets.name: reference-matcher
assets.purpose: Independently authored naive O(n^2) price-time-priority matching engine. Deliberately simple (correctness over speed) so it shares no code path with the optimized implementation under test.

assets.name: seeded-lob-replay
assets.purpose: Deterministic seeded order-flow generator + recorded replay fixtures. Each seed produces a reproducible stream of limit/market/cancel orders driving the differential comparison.

raytracer-calib.description: Ray-tracer rendering oracle used only to calibrate the gate harness (not as a pass/fail gate for shipped work). Renders a fixed scene and issues a verdict by comparing output against a reference image via SSIM at a high similarity threshold.

assets.name: reference-render
assets.purpose: Golden reference render of the calibration scene at fixed resolution/seed. The verdict gate scores the implementation's render against this image with SSIM.

team-copilot.description: Unified team co-piloting oracle (REDUM TEAM-LENS arm). Folds an identical seeded teammate work-state stream through the REAL redum team lens (bin/lib/redum.factor_for_task with team_lens=True, driven over a real on-disk claim+checkpoint ledger) and an independently-authored reference fold, normalizes both to a common comparable partition (the team-candidate roster [surface, haid, human, class, adoptable] — NOT the raw records), and asserts they are identical across all seeds. Catches whole-aggregate co-piloting bugs a per-record property check passes: a cross-team read (RT-ISO), a reaped-vs-in-flight misclassification (RT-CLASS, the code∪work bridge: don't-reinvent live work / don't-redo dropped work), a dropped teammate row (RT-DROP), or a teammate's goal prose leaking into a surfaced candidate (RT-LEAK). The team residual signal at the commit gate is WARN-only (never blocks); the local same-repo redum duplicate gate is unchanged (still hard-blocks).

assets.name: reference-fold
assets.purpose: Independently authored, spec-only recomputation of the team-candidate roster over a seeded teammate work-state stream. Imports nothing from bin/lib/* (every rule reproduced from INVARIANTS.md), so it shares no code path with the implementation under test (bin/lib/redum.py team lens).

assets.name: seeded-workstate-stream
assets.purpose: Deterministic seeded teammate work-state stream generator (reference.generate_stream). Same seed => byte-identical stream; the distribution exercises all three classes (in-flight / adoptable-dropped / completed) plus a cross-team slice that must be excluded (RT-ISO).

symbol-reuse.description: Cross-project symbol-reuse oracle (ponytail rung-2: 'already exists? reuse it'). Folds an identical seeded stream of symbol declarations through the implementation detector (bin/lib/redum.detect_symbol_reuse, via synthesized source) and an independently-authored reference fold, normalizes both to a common comparable partition (the blocked/advised/ok classification — NOT the raw findings), and asserts they are identical across all seeds. Catches whole-partition classification bugs a per-symbol property check passes: a missed exact function/type re-declaration (SR-C/SR-D), a false-flagged unique symbol (SR-H), an ignored opt-out marker (SR-B), or a cross-file duplicate missed by a file-local index (the project-wide guarantee).

assets.name: reference-fold
assets.purpose: Independently authored, spec-only recomputation of the symbol-reuse classification over a seeded synthetic symbol-declaration stream. Imports nothing from bin/lib/* (every rule reproduced from INVARIANTS.md), so it shares no code path with the implementation under test.

assets.name: seeded-symbol-stream
assets.purpose: Deterministic seeded symbol-declaration stream generator (reference.generate_stream). Same seed => byte-identical stream; the distribution cycles eight class templates so every seed exercises blocked (exact fn/type), advised (structural/same-name/const), ok (unique + opt-out), and dropped (ignored path).
